html:
The Iran-backed Houthis have claimed major advances in Yemen, seizing control of key Red Sea shipping lanes including Perim Island and the port of Mokha. This rapid expansion, described as an "unprecedented threat," prompted Saudi Arabia to shut down its East-West oil pipeline after multiple Houthi attacks, escalating the ongoing Iran war and raising global concerns over oil prices and trade.

Great-Power Politics/Iran War: Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth defended the Iran war on the 25th anniversary of 9/11. An Iranian security source suggests Trump seeks negotiations, even as Iran's president describes pressure as "critical and dangerous." Iran, pursuing "cautious escalation," plans to discuss the Strait of Hormuz with Gulf states. North Korea accelerates its nuclear program, solidifying alliances with Russia and China; Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats.

Global Economy & Energy: The Houthi seizure of Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandab Strait, directly threatens global trade and oil prices. Saudi Arabia has already shut down its East-West crude oil pipeline after multiple Houthi attacks. Beyond the Middle East, the US-Canada trade war creates difficulties for auto-parts makers, while sanctions impact Iran, where many are losing jobs amid rising unemployment. Iran also reportedly routed billions via a China sanctions workaround.

Wars and Security: Beyond Yemen, Israel destroyed a major underground Hezbollah base in South Lebanon, causing a 4.1 magnitude shockwave, as UN peacekeepers accompany NPR behind Israeli lines following a US-brokered ceasefire. Russia is again drawing near to Izium, a frontline city fearing "obliteration," and targeting Ukrainian military facilities in Kyiv. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Trump to impose new Russia sanctions, while Russia employs tactics to disqualify parliamentary election candidates.

China and Human Rights: In Hong Kong, activists who organized annual commemorations of the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown have been sentenced to up to seven years in prison under Beijing's national security law. This move is widely seen as a barometer of the city's eroding freedoms, as Hong Kong was previously one of the only places in Chinese territory where the crackdown could be openly marked.

US Domestic & International Affairs: Donald Trump continues to tout $5,000 payments if Republicans retain Congress, a promise some in his party question. US President Donald Trump used his 9/11 remarks at the Pentagon to defend the Iran war. A Trump ally, Joe diGenova, resigned from an inquiry into alleged conspiracy. The company for the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool makeover reportedly admitted flaws, contradicting Trump’s vandalism claims. A Republican US Senate candidate, Mike Rogers, has sought to implicate Abdul El-Sayed over 9/11, despite twice voting against benefits for first responders.

Other Global Developments: Elsewhere, scientists report August was Earth's hottest month on record, largely due to human-caused climate change. A global report warns that one in nine migratory birds is threatened with extinction. Norway's Princess Astrid died, and children have died in a school fire in Bukavu, Democratic Republic of Congo.
